title: Geometric chirp MgF2/HfO2 stack with thickness ratio template and HfO2 cap
scientific_hypothesis: A geometric progression thickness template (ratio r∈[1.08,1.12]) with 85nm HfO2 upper bound will produce candidates with higher UV transmission by pre-filtering absorption-dominated thick-HfO2 configurations, enabling the optimizer to focus computational budget on stopband engineering within feasible transmission windows.
design_principle: Replace free-parameter initialization with geometric progression template for both high- and low-index layers to enforce physically realistic chirp gradient. HfO2 thickness cap prevents deep-UV absorption losses while maintaining visible/NIR rejection capability.
proposed_topology: 20-layer alternating stack: air | [MgF2 | HfO2]_10 | fused_silica substrate. Exact layer count: 20 finite layers.
design_variables: layer thicknesses with geometric progression initialization r∈[1.08,1.12]
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 thickness capped at 85nm for UV transparency
geometric chirp reproducible via calibrated deposition rate
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for coherent multilayer interference
Geometric progression chirp for broadband stopband expansion
expected_advantages: Systematic chirp gradient improves visible/NIR rejection bandwidth
Initialization template guides optimizer toward physically feasible region
known_risks: Geometric constraint may limit optimal thickness combinations
85nm HfO2 cap may reduce stopband depth if insufficient optical thickness
execution_request_english: Design a 20-layer alternating MgF2/HfO2 planar multilayer filter on fused silica substrate for normal incidence. Initialize layer thicknesses using geometric progression with ratio r sampled uniformly from [1.08, 1.12] for both MgF2 and HfO2 layers. Enforce hard upper bound of 85nm on all HfO2 layer thicknesses during initialization and optimization. MgF2 layers may range 20-200nm. Evaluate coherent S-matrix transmittance spectrum from 255-1100nm. Score three objectives: mean transmittance maximization in 255-280nm passband, mean transmittance minimization in 300-700nm visible stopband, mean transmittance minimization in 700-1100nm NIR stopband. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with bound projection. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
revision_reason: Applied feedback directive: replaced free-parameter initialization with geometric progression template (r∈[1.08,1.12]) and imposed 85nm HfO2 upper bound to filter absorption-dominated candidates in 255-280nm range.
